papers.title: From a Single RGB Image to Robot Execution: Metric Scene Alignment and Contact-Guided Retargeting
papers.authors: Zhenxuan Ding, Yu Huang, Xinmiao Wang, Chenghao Sun, Ziyang Dong, Wenhao Cui
papers.abstract: Extending humanoid interaction generation to new environments remains limited by the need for prebuilt 3D scene assets. Reconstructing scenes directly from single RGB images offers a way to overcome this limitation, but introduces a key challenge in maintaining geometric consistency throughout motion generation and transfer. Visually plausible human motions may be misaligned with the reconstructed scene, while retargeting can introduce additional support errors due to differences between human and robot embodiments. We present a unified pipeline that transforms a single RGB image into a humanoid motion reference. It reconstructs scene geometry from the input image, generates a human interaction conditioned on the reconstructed scene, and retargets the motion to a humanoid robot. To maintain geometric consistency throughout this process, we incorporate two complementary refinement stages before and after embodiment transfer. Before retargeting, Joint Metric Interaction Refinement (JMIR) refines human motion alignment with the registered metric scene while preserving the generated interaction structure. Following retargeting, Contact Guided Residual Retargeting (CGRR) corrects robot specific support errors to restore the intended support relationships. Together, these stages produce motion references that are consistent with the reconstructed scene and can be followed by multiple pretrained humanoid trackers without scene specific policy fine tuning. Compared with GRAIL, our method reduces refinement time from 480 s to 87 s, yielding a speedup of 5.5 times. The complete pipeline achieves a success rate of 89% in simulation and 70% across 50 physical trials on the Unitree G1, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating executable humanoid motion references from single RGB images.

papers.title: Forward kinematics accuracy enhancement of a force-torque decoupled spherical parallel manipulator near singular configurations within a tripodal robot
papers.authors: David Feller
papers.abstract: Abstract This article presents an extended mechanical design of the general spherical parallel manipulator to enhance the accuracy of the forward kinematics problem subject to measurement inaccuracies with a significant improvement upon the state-of-the-art close to singular configurations. This is achieved through integration of an internal serial structure occupying the unused space within the manipulator centre, which allows to attach a fourth joint sensor collecting partially redundant information. Although this alters the topological structure of the classical 3-RRR mechanism, we utilize a non-overconstrained design comprising an outer 3-CCC shell combined with an inner RRR chain, creating a dedicated force-torque separation which avoids interferences with the conceptual properties of the manipulator. Since the additional measurement axis coincides with the axis sensitive to singular configurations, this allows to salvage fundamentally ill-conditioned postures where the classical three-sensor method is prone to inaccuracies. The set-up is investigated analytically through derivation of the corresponding sensor Jacobian matrix, where the proposed method incorporates a dynamically adjusted attraction coefficient within an optimization problem to avoid overshooting. Verification is conducted through simulation with distorted measurement signals, evaluated by both the classical and proposed methods, illustrating improved reconstruction accuracy and robustness. With the mechanism being part of a serial-parallel, tripodal robot, validation with respect to feasibility, integration and real-time capability is performed on the built prototype. Special methods for inverse and forward kinematics suitable for high-speed applications using spherical trigonometry and spatial vector constructions are implemented and validated, simplifying classical 8th-order polynomial approaches to provide a unique solution through working and assembly mode continuity.

papers.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
papers.authors: Run Wang, Yilin Mo, Liang Wu
papers.abstract: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

papers.title: Failure Recovery in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents: A Structured Review of Detection, Correction, and State Consistency
papers.authors: Ravi Shanker Thadishetti, Vidya Manyam
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language model agents increasingly act on the world through tools such as code interpreters, application programming interfaces, search engines, perception modules and robotic planners. Every tool call is an opportunity for failure: the model may choose the wrong tool, write malformed input, misread a returned value, trust an erroneous output, or leave external systems in a half-changed condition after a partial sequence of actions. This paper is a structured, qualitative review of how the literature detects such failures, corrects them and keeps the state of the agent and its environment consistent while doing so. It adapts the feedback-loop model and the loud/silent distinction of Sun et al. (2024) to organise a taxonomy of failures, groups detection methods into execution signals, output verification, model self-assessment, external critics and human oversight, correction methods into retry, repair, reflection, replanning, rollback and escalation, and consistency mechanisms into idempotency, compensating actions, checkpointing, action logging, state verification and memory hygiene. A study-by-study comparison of nine representative works, including 2025–2026 studies, records their methods, benchmarks, findings, limitations and treatment of state consistency. Within the reviewed corpus, explicit error messages are comparatively well exploited, silent failures appear to remain a major open problem, self-correction without external feedback is reported to be unreliable on reasoning tasks, and state consistency receives less attention than detection and correction. The paper closes with recommendations for evaluation and design and an agenda for future research. The review is not exhaustive and reports no new experiments.

papers.title: FOE-Dreamer: Deployment-Efficient Learning of Cyber Defense Policies in Operational Networks
papers.authors: Yinuo Du, Christopher Kiekintveld
papers.abstract: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.

papers.abstract: Abstract Automated surgical video analysis serves as the critical foundation for surgical embodied intelligence. However, privacy regulations and data-sharing restrictions pose significant challenges to its collaborative development in computer-assisted surgery. While federated learning (FL) offers a decentralized approach, it remains vulnerable to privacy breaches and single-point failures due to its reliance on a central server. Here, we propose a blockchain-based federated learning (BFL) framework for secure and collaborative surgical video analysis. BFL integrates blockchain’s decentralized consensus and encryption mechanisms with collaborative learning, eliminating the need for a central coordinator. The framework employs cross-validation guided parameter encryption and dynamic weight aggregation to safeguard data privacy, and adopts a hybrid model architecture ''shared + private'' to balance global generalization with local personalization. We apply BFL to distributed surgical video analysis environments involving both medical center and perspective heterogeneity, using data collected from multiple medical centers. Experimental results show that BFL outperforms traditional federated learning methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness. Overall, by establishing a trustworthy model for collaborative medical AI, our framework facilitates secure data sharing across medical centers, empowering surgical embodied intelligence with the visual perception essential for future autonomous surgical assistance.

papers.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
papers.authors: Qi Zhang, Bohan Wang, Qianru Sun, Hanwang Zhang
papers.abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulation tasks such as mental rotation, paper folding, and perspective taking, and is not explained by task difficulty, reasoning depth, or sequential update load. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway also encodes spatial information in a higher-rank, probe-decodable form, but is not the causal handle. To separate decodability from causal use, we analyze concentration, alignment, and semantic location. These diagnostics explain why behavior, probing, and intervention can diverge. Multimodal training thus reshapes the geometry of text-only reasoning, not just how visual input is processed.

papers.title: Embedded Sim-to-Real Visual Servoing: Learned Reaching and Force-Guided Placement
papers.authors: Dezhi Sun, Duy Khang Banh, Kenan Niu
papers.abstract: Embedded perception-to-control systems must combine visual targeting with reliable contact handling under tight computational constraints. We present a shared architecture on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin controlling a Franka Research 3 through Cartesian impedance control. RealSense D435i observations, YOLO11-seg segmentation, depth back-projection, and hand--eye calibration provide metric robot-frame targets. We compare two strategies: compact proximal policy optimization (PPO) policies transferred from simulation for object- and hole-region reaching, and force-guided Cartesian placement using approximately 2 N normal contact and spiral search. The PPO policies achieved 87.2% and 83.1% success over 1000 simulation episodes each. Across 50 real-robot trials per strategy, the learned hybrid and force-guided analytical pipelines achieved 70.0% and 74.0% completion, respectively. Mean perception latency with TensorRT was 34.55 ms. These results support an embedded architecture combining learned free-space reaching with explicit contact correction.

papers.title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies
papers.authors: Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Xingyu Ren, Haizhao Yang
papers.abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

papers.title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
papers.authors: Zenghui Yang, Xinan Wang, Danyang Li, Zhe Xu, Zheng Yang, Jingao Xu, Qiang Ma
papers.abstract: Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the basic units of both environmental understanding and computation. EMS-Nav groups objects and their relationships into functionally meaningful spaces and builds a hierarchy from local areas to the broader environment. This organization supports efficient map construction alongside the interpretation and execution of language goals at different scales. In multi-scale navigation experiments, EMS-Nav achieves the highest success rates across all four target categories: objects, rooms, regions, and specific instances. It outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping and navigation methods, improving overall first-attempt success by 9.39 percentage points over the strongest baseline while reducing mapping overhead and language-model input size. Local deployment in real indoor environments further demonstrates its applicability to on-device embodied navigation. By establishing regions as the organizing basis for perception, spatial understanding, and language-guided action, EMS-Nav provides a system that combines multi-scale understanding with computational efficiency to support diverse language goals on resource-constrained robots.

papers.title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation
papers.authors: Ivan Valuev, Iana Zhura, Valerii Serpiva, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou
papers.abstract: We present DroneDiffusion, a perception-aware diffusion planner for local 3-D UAV trajectory generation that explicitly models and avoids failure zones caused by lens flare, overexposure, and reflective surfaces. A vision-language perceptual safety estimator produces a pixel-aligned reliability map that highlights regions of degraded sensing. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is conditioned on this map together with the onboard RGB image, goal point, and initial velocity to generate egocentric 3-D trajectories. To enforce obstacle avoidance at inference time without retraining, we apply training-free CHOMP guidance over a 3-D Euclidean signed distance field. The model is trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot on a real drone. Reliability conditioning raises the mean perceptual reliability along generated trajectories to 0.71, compared with 0.63 for a geometric baseline, while guidance halves the collision rate of the learned prior from 14.7% to 7.8%. Perceptual safety conditioning and geometric guidance are therefore complementary: treating sensor reliability as a first-class signal reduces incursions into unreliable regions while maintaining competitive navigation performance.

papers.title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?
papers.authors: Ayush Gaggar, Jared Berry, Todd D. Murphey
papers.abstract: Embodied world models (WMs) are implicit learning systems that predict the next future latent state directly from observations and actions. Unique from other end-to-end learning systems, the dynamics predictor of WMs can simulate the environment's response to alternative actions without physical deployment nor pre-specifying states of the dynamical system. Current metrics focus on the quality of model outputs, e.g., clarity of reconstructions or task success, but fail to assess the fidelity of modeling consequences of counterfactual actions. Inspecting the forced response to action perturbations through sensitivity analysis is one way to audit how well WMs can predict the consequences of counterfactual actions. Deploying WMs on hardware will require new evaluation frameworks to analyze the tradeoffs between state error and accurate sensitivity prediction.

papers.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
papers.authors: Liman Wang, Hanyang Zhong, Sun Zhaole, Wenting Cao, Babar Jamil, Andy Tyrrell, Shan Luo, Jihong Zhu
papers.abstract: Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics. We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval. To make multi-finger force observations easier to fuse, we express fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame, giving force components consistent geometric meaning across fingers and time. Using an Action Chunking Transformer backbone, policies fuse multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage. Across these evaluations, the learned policies achieve consistent removal performance, and ablations show that wrist-frame forces, especially with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over local-frame force inputs and no-force baselines. papers.title: Development and Weighting of a Task-Nurse-Nursing Robot Fit Indicator System and a Three-Dimensional Fit Calculation Framework for Biosafety Emergency Response: A Delphi and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process Study
papers.authors: Chao Wu, Ting Song, Jiayi Zhang, Jiaqi Yuan, Yawei Lin, Zhen Sa, Nan Li, Cong Ren
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective To develop a task-nurse-nursing robot fit indicator system for biosafety emergency response, determine the relative weights of indicators at each level, and propose an operational three-dimensional fit calculation framework as a basis for developing and validating a task-matching assessment tool. Methods An initial indicator framework was developed through theoretical analysis, literature review, and qualitative interviews. A two-round Delphi survey of 15 experts was conducted to screen and revise the indicators, and Kendall's coefficient of concordance (W) was used to assess agreement among the experts. Fuzzy analytic hierarchy process was then used to construct aggregate judgment matrices, calculate indicator weights, and assess matrix compatibility. A conceptual fit calculation framework was further developed for three candidate execution modes: nurse-only, nursing robot-only, and nurse-robot collaborative execution. The framework was based on requirement-capability mapping, weighted capability deficits, and safety veto rules. Results The initial framework comprised 3 first-level, 10 second-level, and 23 third-level indicators; after two Delphi rounds, the final system comprised 3 first-level, 9 second-level, and 36 third-level indicators. The valid response rate was 100% in both rounds, and the expert authority coefficient was 0.907. Kendall's W values for the first-, second-, and third-level indicators were 0.325, 0.313, and 0.338 in round 1 and 0.496, 0.386, and 0.386 in round 2, respectively (all P < 0.01), indicating good expert agreement. The initial weights of the first-level indicators were 0.3822 for nursing task characteristics, 0.3522 for nurse capabilities, and 0.2656 for nursing robot performance. The compatibility indices of all aggregate judgment matrices were < 0.1. Based on the indicators and weights, a three-dimensional fit decision process comprising requirement-capability mapping, hard-constraint screening, capability-deficit calculation, and ranking of candidate execution modes was proposed. Conclusion This study developed a preliminary task-nurse-nursing robot fit indicator system, relative indicator weights, and a conceptual fit calculation framework. The aggregate judgment matrices demonstrated acceptable internal compatibility. The framework provides a computable pathway for developing a task-matching assessment tool; however, the mapping relationships, rating anchors, thresholds, measurement properties, and practical scheduling utility require further calibration and validation through simulation exercises and multicenter studies.

papers.title: Designing Piano Technique: A Historical and Industrial Design Analysis of Piano-Playing Aids From 1814 to the Present
papers.authors: Burcu Torum
papers.abstract: This study examines piano-playing aids documented from 1814 to the present from an industrial design history perspective.Thirty-four product configurations, documented through October 2026 and identified from patents, method books, period advertisements, museum records, manufacturers' documentation, and academic publications, were compared in terms of problem framing, bodily intervention, adjustability, feedback, skill transfer, and type of evidence.The findings show that these aids did not develop linearly from mechanical to digital technologies.Physical guides, resistance devices, silent practice keyboards, ergonomic adaptations, accessibility systems, computational feedback, and robotic prototypes instead embody different historical design approaches within the same product field.The study conceptualizes these products as materialized pedagogy, through which pedagogical ideas are translated into material or computational features.The principal historical transformation was an expansion of intervention across the body, instrument, interface, and instructional system.The results indicate that technical function, pedagogical claim, and scientific evidence should be distinguished, while user autonomy, bodily diversity, accessibility, and skill transfer should be evaluated together.The study accordingly proposes a conceptual qualitative industrial design evaluation framework for piano-playing aids, illustrated through three cases but not empirically validated.

papers.title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
papers.authors: Yuxuan Feng, Fujing Xie, Sören Schwertfeger, Hermann Blum
papers.abstract: Open-world navigation requires a robot to locate a user-specified target in an indoor scene under open-vocabulary queries. Realistic indoor environments are semi-static: walls and furniture largely persist while smaller objects move, relocate, or vanish between visits. Prior-map systems answer queries from object poses recorded at reconstruction time, which expire as soon as objects move, whereas online methods re-derive where to look from current observations every few steps, often through expensive calls to a vision--language model. Assuming that walls and large furniture do not move, we keep their map to plan paths, but use a target--furniture co-occurrence prior to decide where to search. We present PreNav, an ObjectNav framework on semi-static environments. Rather than invoking a vision-language model at each step, PreNav generates a single global search reference before the robot moves: an LLM converts target--furniture co-occurrence into a spatial prior, a conditional diffusion model turns that prior and the persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it, and the robot approaches the target once it is detected online. Experiments on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark show that PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors, using a generator trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries further validate the approach.

papers.title: Da Vinci Xi robotic-assisted surgery for gastrointestinal stromal tumors: analysis of 20 mexican cases with regard to tumor size and location
papers.authors: Luis Enrique García-Rios, Marisol Luna-Castillo, Erick A. Lopez-Herrera, Ma. Guadalupe J. De Anda-González, Rafael Medrano Guzman
papers.abstract: Background: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) require R0 surgical resection as the standard treatment. Robotic surgery emerges as a promising alternative in complex cases, although no published series exist in Latin America. Objectives: The objective of the study was to evaluate robotic surgery in the treatment of GIST and the impact of tumor size and location on surgical outcomes. Materials and methods: Retrospective observational cohort study at the Oncology Hospital, Centro Médico Nacional Siglo XXI, Mexico City. Twenty patients with GIST underwent robotic surgery (da Vinci Xi) between January 2022 and December 2024, with follow-up until March 2025. Results: Mean age 65.2 years (10 men and 10 women). R0 resection was achieved in 100%, conversion rate to open surgery 5%, mean intraoperative blood loss was 101 mL, mean hospital stay 6.3 days, mean tumor size 5.47 cm, and post-operative morbidity 15%. Median follow-up 19 months: disease-free survival 100%. Conclusion: Robotic resection of GIST in technically complex cases was safe and feasible in this first Mexican series.

papers.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning
papers.authors: Yike Qiao, Xiaodong He, An Zhuo, Zhiyong Sun, Weimin Bao, Zhongkui Li
papers.abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start. Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region. Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals. Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities. Hardware experiments on a ground vehicle further demonstrate collision-free convergence across different targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.

papers.title: CrowdMAPS: Crowdsourcing Multiple Actions per State for Real-World Imitation Learning
papers.authors: Yilong Song, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Karthik Desingh, Chen Zhu-Tian
papers.abstract: Real-world robot imitation learning is often limited by the cost of collecting physical demonstrations, which typically yield only one action label per visited state. We present CrowdMAPS, a web-based crowdsourcing paradigm for augmenting real-robot datasets with Multiple Actions per State (MAPS). After or during standard robot data collection, CrowdMAPS distributes visited robot states to remote annotators through a web-based 3D interface, where they specify alternative valid actions without requiring access to physical robot hardware. This expands robot datasets along a complementary "width" dimension--by increasing the number of actions per visited state--rather than only by collecting more trajectories. We evaluate CrowdMAPS using keyframe-centric goal-pose annotations supplied by non-expert annotators and train imitation policies on the resulting MAPS data. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, increasing MAPS width from one to ten actions per state improves sample efficiency and increases average success rates by 35.6 percentage points for keypose policies and 33.0 percentage points for trajectory policies. These results show that software-mediated human annotations can augment physical robot data to afford denser supervision, establishing CrowdMAPS as a scalable digital layer for real-robot data collection.

papers.title: Cross-domain safety standards for semi-autonomous powered wheelchairs: a comparative analysis and harmonisation framework
papers.authors: Stanley Chong, David A. McMeekin, Siavash Khaksar, Iain D. Murray
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Semi-autonomous powered wheelchairs combine user control with autonomous navigation and offer substantial benefits for users with vision impairments and older adults, but their safe deployment is hindered by fragmented safety standards spanning the medical device, automotive and robotics domains. No unified framework addresses their requirements. This paper determines which safety requirements for this device class are satisfied by existing standards, which are satisfied only partially, and which are absent altogether. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twelve international standards and frameworks relevant to semi-autonomous wheelchair safety were identified through systematic domain mapping across four sectors. Seven were subjected to full comparative scoring against a 36-dimension requirement framework adapted from UNECE NATM/FRAV automated-driving requirements, using a four-level coverage scale applied independently by four raters and reconciled to consensus. RESULTS: Seven significant gaps in current standards coverage, including the absence of requirements for autonomous navigation in assistive contexts, inappropriate controllability assumptions for users with impairments, undefined shared control safety requirements, and inadequate provisions for vulnerable user populations. Four gaps are classified as critical priority and three as high priority. Root causes are identified for each gap, and bridging potential is assessed from existing standards. CONCLUSIONS: This work provides the first cross-domain gap analysis for semi-autonomous assistive mobility and establishes a foundation for the development of harmonised safety standards. The findings have immediate implications for standards bodies, manufacturers and regulators seeking to enable safe market access for this beneficial technology.

papers.title: Connectome-derived structural support identifies a compact scaffold for robust embodied control in BIOSEED
papers.authors: Pantaleone Carlucci, Giorgia Ghergo, Lucia Paciucci
papers.abstract: Abstract Biological nervous systems combine sparse connectivity with structured recurrent organization, but it remains unclear whether such structure can serve as a functional prior for artificial embodied control. Here we use BIOSEED, a bounded food/toxin foraging framework, to test whether connectome-derived structural support has behaviorally consequential value under controlled perturbations and learned-controller controls. A staged audit demotes historical shuffled/random controls to fixed-support perturbations, shows that corrected density-matched binary rewiring collapses performance, verifies transfer across implemented environmental shifts, and shows that causal lesions degrade the TRUE structure. A compact top-in 10% scaffold is statistically non-inferior to the full topology in locked validation and transfer, so 85% of the connectome-derived edges can be removed at no behavioral cost. Matched non-biological reductions of equal sparsity reach at most about two thirds of the full-topology score, and connectome-derived selections based on out-degree or synaptic weight also fail, so the sufficiency is specific to incoming-connectivity structure rather than to sparsity or connectome provenance alone. Learned MLP/RNN/GRU controls show that the task is learnable and that intake can be increased, including by a compact GRU approaching the conservative band; however, they do not reduce the scaffold result to a trivial optimization artifact. Live and rover-style demonstrations provide secondary closed-loop diagnostics. BIOSEED therefore identifies a connectome-derived structural prior for conservative embodied control within the tested framework.

papers.title: Clinical-priority task orchestration and verified safety supervision for a physician-directed ward-rounding robot: a simulation-based feasibility study
papers.authors: Cheng Hang, Safaa Najah Saud Al-Humairi, Ahgalya Subbiah
papers.abstract: Introduction A ward-rounding robot that accepts orders at the level of clinical intent becomes a shared clinical resource: several clinicians may hold outstanding requests of differing urgency, and execution is punctuated by confirmation gates at which the robot waits on a human and by engagement steps that cannot safely be interrupted. This paper formalizes the resulting scheduling problem together with the safety layer that it necessitates. Methods We present (i) a task model in which an intent-level order expands into primitives carrying resource locks, physician confirmation gates, and an explicit interruptibility partition; (ii) the Clinical-Priority Scheduler (CP-Sched), which combines urgency weighting, aging, travel awareness, and class-relative escalation and preempts only at safe interruption points; and (iii) a safety supervisor specified as a network of timed automata and verified exhaustively for a single robot serving one order at a time, with independent reproduction in the TLA+ model checker TLC. All task timings in the 1,590 discrete-event simulation runs are modeling assumptions, not hardware measurements. Results Across 1,080 runs spanning two ward sizes and three utilization levels, CP-Sched reduced the 95th-percentile time for urgent orders to bedside from 347 s to 215 s at moderate utilization, a 38% reduction relative to the strongest of four baselines; all comparisons survived Holm’s correction at p < 0.0001 under both the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and unpaired Mann–Whitney tests (rank-biserial effect sizes: 0.93–1.00 paired, 0.66–0.93 unpaired). A further 510 runs showed that aging alone cannot bound the waiting time and that escalation at a fixed absolute horizon restores a guarantee only by inflating the urgent tail at saturation. All five clinical invariants hold under the supervisor and each is violable without it, so none is vacuous. Runtime enforcement eliminated all 757 unsafe interruptions observed in the unshielded ablation at a cost of 2.1–35.4 s in the median urgent tail. Discussion The enforcement cost is small but systematic at light and moderate loads and undetectable at saturation, which supports keeping the safety layer independent of the scheduling policy. The formal guarantee covers a single-order model, and absolute timings require calibration on a physical platform.

papers.title: Can I join you? Extended Social Force Based Model with Predictive Control and Barrier Functions for Humanoid Group Repositioning Amidst Obstacles
papers.authors: Chuxuan Zhang, Niloofar Jahanshahi, Yasaman Etesam, Mo Chen, Angelica Lim
papers.abstract: As social and service robots increasingly share interaction spaces in public, they may form groups while coordinating tasks or interacting with humans. Initial group formation alone is insufficient in dynamic settings, because it can be disrupted when a person or another agent joins, leaves, or passes through the group. Although group dynamics and repositioning have been widely studied in swarm robotics and virtual-agent settings, little attention has been given to socially appropriate repositioning behaviors in groups of humanoid robots. Existing social-force-based approaches provide a useful foundation for group behavior, but they have limited obstacle handling, and can produce unsafe behavior as environmental complexity increases. We propose a novel framework that modulates traditional Social Force, guided by Model Predictive Control (MPC) to plan ahead, bounded by Control Barrier Functions (CBF) to increase safety for robot groups repositioning behaviors. This approach aims to produce safer and socially aware group repositioning behaviors under various group formation disturbance. We evaluate the method in simulation through an ablation study and an online user study. The results show that our proposed method can produce smoother and safer repositioning behaviors in complex environments while preserving social appropriateness.

papers.title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
papers.authors: Pengyang Shi, Jinlu Zhang, Chunze Lin, Yizhou Wang, Li Yi
papers.abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy and injects it as an $ε$-space correction. Experiments on BEAT demonstrate best-in-class semantic fidelity (SRGR $0.9916$, FID $27.18$) with GT-level beat alignment (BA $0.1826$ vs. GT $0.1743$), and 76-83% win rate in blind pairwise human evaluation against all prior methods. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid confirms direct sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
papers.authors: Xiao Ma, Yijun Chen, Zhiquan Hu, Jicheng Zhao, Yuming Li, Chuang Dai
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refinement into waypoint residual correction and position-conditioned heading generation. Through imitation learning and a future-token auxiliary task, the backbone provides predictive representations and a base trajectory. The position expert predicts bounded metric waypoint residuals, while the heading expert reconstructs vehicle orientation from adjacent angular increments conditioned on the corrected path. With the backbone frozen, the two experts are optimized alternately through supervised initialization and reinforcement fine-tuning. This design simplifies refinement through clear physical specialization while preserving conditional coupling during prediction and optimization. On NAVSIM v1, CARE-Drive achieves 88.8 PDMS, improving by 2.4 points over the unrefined base trajectories generated by the same backbone. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of specialized experts and staged training.

papers.title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
papers.authors: Chenhao Qiu, Shuyi Chen, Songen Gu, Shufeng Nan, Tianyu Wang, Siyu Lin, Yifan Li, Bingwen Zhu, et al.
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. This raises a critical question: when should a robot policy imagine the future? In this paper, we propose Bind-WAM, a binding-uncertainty-guided WAM for selective future imagination. Bind-WAM introduces language-object binding uncertainty, selectively invoking joint future-action generation when the current observation does not support stable task-relevant action generation. An offline labeling pipeline uses complete demonstrations and action context to identify task-relevant objects and detect reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity drift. The resulting pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight router that predicts binding uncertainty from the current observation and language instruction. At inference, a shared WAM policy invokes selective future imagination according to the predicted uncertainty and its change between consecutive replanning steps. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that Bind-WAM can establish binding uncertainty as a strong, interpretable signal for selective future imagination.

papers.title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Kun Chu, Xufeng Zhao, Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter
papers.abstract: Bimanual robotic manipulation is versatile, yet its central challenge lies not only in executing dexterous motion with each hand, but also in coordinating the two arms for long-horizon manipulation under coupled spatial and temporal constraints. Prior work has largely focused on endowing robots with human-level manipulation skills, paying less attention to the structure of bimanual behaviour itself: many practical tasks are a coordinated composition of reusable unimanual skills and a small set of synchronous bimanual skills. This makes high-level spatio-temporal coordination, rather than skill acquisition alone, a key bottleneck for efficient bimanual execution. We propose BiPOP, a framework that couples Large Language Models (LLMs) with Temporal Partial-Order Planning for long-horizon bimanual manipulation. At its core is an explicit spatio-temporal model that partitions the workspace by arm reachability and captures inter-arm dependencies, arm assignment, synchronization requirements, and opportunities for safe concurrent execution. Building on this model, an LLM translates natural-language instructions into a formal PDDL specification, while a temporal planner enforces the constraints and schedules actions, yielding plans that are logically consistent at the symbolic level and efficient through parallel execution. On simulated long-horizon tasks of varying complexity, BiPOP outperforms open-loop planning with strong reasoning models and closed-loop ReAct-style planning in success rate, planning time, and plan efficiency, and the full pipeline runs end to end on the real bimanual robot NICOL. A failure analysis further shows that LLM-only planners mainly violate spatial and temporal coordination constraints, which motivates delegating these constraints to a symbolic planner. papers.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
papers.authors: Fabian Jenelten, Deepana Ishtaweera, Pablo Garcia, Liana Margolese, Igor Bogoslavskyi, Luca Buonocore, Jan Migliazza, Aleksandrs Ecins, et al.
papers.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

papers.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather
papers.authors: Eren Erdal Aksoy, Abu Mohammed Raisuddin, Thien-Thu Ngo, Eren Aydemir, Osman Tahir Ekşi, Paula Litkey, Petri Manninen, Heikki Hyyti, et al.
papers.abstract: Automated driving has gained remarkable momentum over the past decade, with both industry and academia investing substantial resources in developing perception and control solutions to advance vehicle autonomy. However, these efforts have largely focused on clear-weather scenarios, leaving harsh conditions, such as snow, rain, and fog, comparatively understudied. As a result, inclement weather remains one of the most significant hurdles for autonomous vehicles, often leading to substantial performance degradation in downstream perception and control tasks. In this paper, we present insights from the EU-funded Horizon Europe project ROADVIEW, which aims to develop robust, weather-aware perception and control modules for connected and automated vehicles operating under severe conditions, including snow, rain, and fog. Drawing on four years of large-scale development and real-world demonstrations across multiple vehicle platforms in different locations, we identify ten key challenges that hinder the development of weather-resilient autonomy, including data scarcity, domain shifts, limitations in multimodal perception, control robustness, and validation gaps, among others. We summarize these challenges and lessons learned toward enabling reliable snow-autonomous driving, highlighting critical directions for future research and standardization.

papers.title: AquaMamba: Selective state space modeling for underwater scene segmentation in marine robotics
papers.authors: Shuxi Chen, Jianlin Qiu, Yiyang Sun, Haifei Zhang, Hao Chen
papers.abstract: Underwater scene segmentation is challenging because image degradation and domain shift vary greatly in marine environments, and the behavior of selective state-space models (SSMs) in this environment remains insufficiently characterized. We propose AquaMamba, a ResNet34-UNet segmentation framework that replaces the bottleneck operator with stacked Mamba layers, and compare it with five established CNN-based methods and a constructed Transformer-bottleneck baseline in the SUIM benchmark. AquaMamba achieves an mIoU of 0.669, 1.9 percentage points higher than the controlled Trans-UNet baseline (0.650), while using fewer parameters (29.5M vs. 33.9M). DeepLabV3 + remains the strongest overall model, reaching 0.712 mIoU. On the unlabeled UIEB dataset, AquaMamba shows the highest confidence retention among four representative models, retaining 93.5% of its source-domain prediction confidence. Due to the lack of semantic annotation in UIEB, this result reflects prediction confidence rather than target-domain segmentation accuracy. Scale- and boundary-specific diagnostics within the selected representative subset further show complementary behavior among AquaMamba, Trans-UNet and DeepLabV3 + : AquaMamba is competitive in several large object categories and obtains the lowest boundary error point estimate, while DeepLabV3 + remains stronger for human divers and plant/seagrass, and AquaMamba is limited on the reported small-RO subset. These findings position AquaMamba as a controlled SSM baseline for underwater semantic segmentation and emphasize the need for future SSM designs to better integrate multi-scale and high-resolution features.

papers.title: AgriTech: Foundations, Emerging Technologies, System Architectures, and Deployment Readiness—A Comprehensive Survey
papers.authors: IBRAHIM ADABARA, Abdussalam Adamu Jega, Yale Ibrahim Danjuma, Elhadi Abdalla A. Arbab, Ainamukama Anold, Joe Mutebi, Mugisha Brian, kanyesigye simon
papers.abstract: Agricultural technology (AgriTech) is transforming agricultural production through advances in artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, robotics, remote sensing, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support systems. Despite these developments, the transition from technological innovation to effective agricultural deployment remains constrained by technical, operational, economic, and institutional challenges. Existing research frequently emphasizes individual technologies, applications, or performance indicators, providing limited integration of system architectures, operational reliability, affordability, interoperability, and deployment readiness. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of AgriTech foundations, enabling technologies, architectural approaches, agricultural applications, and performance evaluation methods. It examines centralized, distributed, cloud, edge, and hybrid architectures alongside intelligent agricultural systems and autonomous technologies. A comparative analysis identifies their capabilities, limitations, infrastructure requirements, and operational trade-offs. The survey further investigates agricultural data quality, environmental variability, cybersecurity, maintenance, financial sustainability, digital inclusion, and governance challenges affecting practical implementation. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes the Integrated AgriTech Effectiveness and Deployment Readiness Framework (IAEDRF), which connects agricultural requirements, technology selection, system integration, performance validation, economic feasibility, organizational preparedness, and responsible governance. The framework introduces context-dependent assessment criteria, mandatory deployment requirements, and continuous operational reassessment. Its proposed suitability model remains conceptual and requires empirical validation. Finally, the survey identifies research priorities involving generalizable agricultural AI, interoperable infrastructures, affordable technologies, real-world benchmarking, and sustainable scaling. The findings emphasize that AgriTech effectiveness depends not only on technological capability but also on reliable, affordable, interoperable, and context-appropriate deployment. The survey provides an integrated foundation for future research, technology development, and evidence-based agricultural implementation.

papers.title: AeroTea-VLM: a UAV-assisted multimodal visual language model for intelligent disease and pest management in terraced tea plantations
papers.authors: Ziyuan Liu, Xue Li, Yunling Zeng, Xingzhi Zou, Xuanrong Zhang
papers.abstract: Abstract Current vision-language models (VLMs) that are used for UAV agricultural inspection encounter significant challenges. These problems come from scale distortion when drones fly at different heights, and also from really long delays that happen during visual action planning. In this paper, we introduce AeroTea-VLM, which fixes these issues by using a special new idea called "heavy perception, light control." To make sure perception stays the same regardless of scale in 3D terraced farm areas, we came up with two new methods: Altitude-Aware Position Encoding (Alt-PE) and Cross-Altitude Topological Attention (CATA). These two methods work together by adding real-time altimeter and depth data, which helps cut down on feature aliasing problems. For how the drone moves around, our Embodied Chain-of-Action (CoA) module gets rid of the slow autoregressive image generation step. Instead, it just outputs text commands directly. This change cuts total end-to-end delay by 86.5% (down to 385 ms), and it also keeps peak GPU memory usage at 14.2 GB. We tested this whole system on a new dataset that we collected ourselves, which we call AeroTea-Multimodal RGB-D. The tests show that AeroTea-VLM gets 88.5% accuracy when identifying plant diseases, and has an 84.2% success rate on reasoning tasks. Both of these numbers are better than what existing baseline methods can get.

papers.title: Advances in technologies across the marine plastic value chain in Europe: A critical review

papers.abstract: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. MPP has become increasingly widespread across oceans, along coastlines and on the seafloor, resulting in an urgent need for the development of technologies capable of advancing a Circular Economy (CE) for marine-derived products. Advances in cleaner production technologies, including satellite and drone-based remote sensing, autonomous robotic platforms, and machine-vision systems, have improved the efficiency of plastic debris identification, classification, and recovery in complex marine environments. Similarly, innovations in downstream sorting, such as electrostatic separation, selective dissolution, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven classification, are enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of processing MPP. The review evaluates mechanical recycling methods with particular emphasis on recent advances in extrusion, moulding technologies, and additive manufacturing for converting MPP into high-value secondary materials in a CE framework in Europe. These technological developments demonstrate the potential for establishing viable and scalable valorisation routes. Overall, the review outlines key opportunities to strengthen a sustainable CE and guide future research and industrial adoption. In doing so, it provides a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art technologies across the entire marine plastics value chain in Europe, from detection and recovery to separation, identification, and recycling.

papers.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
papers.authors: Dimitrios Chatziparaschis, Georgios Georgakis, Adnan I. Ansar, Shehryar Khattak, Konstantinos Karydis
papers.abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

papers.title: Actuation and Control of Passive Tendon-Driven Soft Extensions Through Rigid Manipulator Motion
papers.authors: Ignacio Cuiral-Zueco, Gonzalo López-Nicolás, Youcef Mezouar
papers.abstract: Industrial manipulators offer reach and precision but can damage nearby structures in confined spaces. Soft robots provide compliant contact but typically have limited reach. Rigid-soft systems combine their advantages, although they often require dedicated actuation and control hardware. We propose actuating a passive tendon-driven soft extension through manipulator joint motion. As the robot moves, the exterior spans of tendons anchored to upstream links change, altering tendon tension and deforming the extension. Inspection through narrow apertures, for example, constrains the motion of the end effector (EE). We develop a controller that regulates the soft tip while preserving such EE constraints. A differential model separates rigid transport from soft deformation, combining analytic arm and tendon kinematics with a locally identified span-to-deformation map. We also derive a local upper bound on the number of independent deformation directions transmitted by the tendons under the EE constraint, and conditions for the exponential convergence of the tip error. A quadratic program with control barrier functions imposes obstacle clearance, fulcrum limits, and model-validity conditions. Simulations and real experiments show tip and shape regulation under free, position-constrained, and fulcrum-constrained EE motion.

papers.title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer
papers.authors: Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Shiduo Zhang, Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Jinqiu Wang, Hang Zhao
papers.abstract: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering. A universal version fitted on 20k hours of data from 24 embodiments averages 8.8 tokens per second for 15 Hz end-effector motion on this corpus. With the same VLA backbone, ActionCodec2 outperforms the compared tokenizers on three simulation benchmarks and in zero-shot real-robot evaluation. Its streaming representation allows policies to incorporate state feedback within an action chunk, substantially improving performance over open-loop execution under randomized dynamics, external disturbances, and moving objects. The same tokens also can serve as a direct control interface for VLM agents, which compose successful action sequences into reusable macros. These agent-built macros reduce control decisions and thinking-token usage across attempts and transfer to a held-out task. More results are available at https://zibindong.github.io/actioncodec2-page/

We present the Autonomous Robotic Translational System (ARTS), an open-source three-arm platform for autonomy research in minimally invasive surgery, built entirely from purchasable parts for about USD 137,000. Two UR5e arms hold wristed da Vinci X/Xi instruments, a UR5 arm holds a stereo endoscope with two FLIR cameras, the surgeon console provides haptic handles, footswitches and a stereo viewer, and a hardware stop independent of the software lets a supervisor freeze all three arms in place. The ROS 2 software pins every dependency, installs from the same scripts on bare metal or in containers, and records stereo images with hardware-measured timing. On the real arms, ARTS commands each arm at its controller's full rate (e.g., 500 Hz on the UR5e), the two cameras expose within 12 microseconds of each other, hand motion reaches the arm in 58 ms, and the endoscope image reaches the monitor in 68 ms. The ISO 9283 pose repeatability is 0.14-0.25 mm, comparable to a da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) Classic arm on the same protocol, and an optical tracker measured a mean remote-center-of-motion error of 0.34-0.37 mm. Three expert and three novice operators performed the Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery (FLS) peg transfer through a laparoscopic trainer box, and one of the experts sutured on a suture pad. papers.title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient
papers.authors: Jinwoo Lee, Geunsik Bae, Changseung Kim, Jiwoo Kim, Woojae Shin, Hyondong Oh
papers.abstract: Vision-based high-speed navigation requires a trajectory planner that can reactively generate smooth, collision-free trajectories from onboard visual observations. Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to vision-based trajectory planning, as it enables the optimization of sequential decision-making policies in complex environments. However, model-free policy gradient methods rely on sample-based policy gradient estimation, which yields noisy gradient estimates and inefficient training. To this end, we propose a framework for learning trajectory planning policies using the analytic policy gradient (APG) method and use it to train APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner. The proposed framework leverages differential flatness to analytically reconstruct vehicle states from planned trajectories, thereby enabling differentiable trajectory-level state transitions without requiring an explicit low-level dynamics model. By iteratively performing trajectory planning and differentiable state transitions, we construct a differentiable episode rollout and analytically compute policy gradients from episode-level losses, improving both training efficiency and policy performance. After approximately 30 minutes of training on a single GPU, APG-Planner demonstrates comparable or superior performance to existing baseline methods in simulation and achieves speeds of up to 11\,m/s in real-world flight experiments. We further validate the proposed framework on a skid-steer ground robot, demonstrating its applicability to differentially flat robotic systems beyond quadrotors.

papers.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI in Medicine: An Autonomy-Centred Scoping Review and Research Agenda
papers.authors: Valentina De Nicolò, Davide La Torre, Ignazio Iacone
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence agents—software systems that perceive, reason, plan and act over multiple steps with limited human intervention—are moving from research prototypes towards clinical deployment. Recent reviews map what has been built; this one asks what would have to hold for such systems to be deployed safely. We conducted a scoping review reported according to the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, searching eight bibliographic sources from January 2017 to June 2026, admitting foundational computer science and regulatory literature alongside clinical applications. Five architectural paradigms recur—tool-augmented large language model agents, multi-agent systems, offline reinforcement learning agents, embodied robotic agents and autonomous monitoring agents—nearly all sharing a common four-layer stack. We introduce a six-level scale of clinical agent autonomy that grades systems by where human judgement enters relative to the reasoning, and by whether the resulting action remains reversible. The scale exposes an inversion in the evidence base: demonstrated patient benefit concentrates at high autonomy in narrow, bounded domains, whereas research effort concentrates at intermediate autonomy, where prospective outcome evidence is absent and automation bias is the dominant risk. We further propose seven evaluation dimensions specific to agency, a mapping of evaluation requirements to autonomy level, and a ten-item failure mode taxonomy assigned to the architectural layer at which each is addressable. Deploying agentic systems safely requires prospective multi-site validation, reporting standards adapted to agency, equity-aware design, and regulatory obligations indexed to autonomy rather than algorithm class. We conclude with an eight-point research agenda.

papers.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
papers.authors: Haoyi Zhang, Qi Zhang, Yunfan Ren, Yi Bin, Lei Zhu, Heng Tao Shen
papers.abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

papers.title: When does online vision-language inference help? A survey of socially aware robot navigation
papers.authors: 박성산, Young-Sik Shin, Sanghyun Kim
papers.abstract: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models are increasingly built into the navigation stacks of robots that share space with people, where the models read cues that occupancy maps omit, such as a raised hand or a conversing group. This survey organizes 41 cases reported from 2024 to 2026, 34 on socially aware navigation and 7 adjacent mechanism extensions, by where the model enters the stack: scene interpretation, cost modulation, subgoal or path proposal, hierarchical coordination, direct action output and offline transfer or generation. For each of these six patterns we describe representative systems and their reported results, and we review the datasets, simulators, benchmarks and metrics behind them. We then discuss what the reported comparisons establish about running the model online, separating system utility, component contribution and online necessity. In these comparisons, cue-aware systems improved the outcomes that hinge on their cue, although whole-system differences limit attribution to the VLM; in one offline study, a model selector helped on hard selections and hurt on routine ones; in one deployment, delayed advice stayed useful when fused with current plans; model-supervised students navigated without runtime teacher queries, but online, cached and distilled alternatives have not been compared with student computation included; and better answers have not yet been linked to better behavior. We also define an invocation ratio (model requests per control decision), propose a minimum reporting set for deployment comparisons, and outline open challenges in real-time reasoning, spatial grounding and safety.

papers.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
papers.authors: Niran Nataraj, Maina Sogabe, Masamichi Yamashita, Norihiko Ito, Kenji Kawashima
papers.abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

papers.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
papers.authors: Qinan Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Qihang Jin, Tianyuan Wang, Hongbing Luo, Pengfei Li, Wenjun Lv, Yu Kang, et al.
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local perception, action-conditioned transitions, presentation stability, representation exchangeability, and Full-CF causal discrimination. Our diagnostic evaluations reveal heterogeneous failure modes, including sensitivity to evidence presentation and encoding, low activation on successful trajectories, and weak paired counterfactual discrimination. Perception-controlled analyses further indicate that visual grounding and objective recovery are substantial, model-dependent bottlenecks. These results motivate jointly reporting correctness, presentation stability, and causal sensitivity instead of relying on a single score.

papers.title: To Bot or not To Bot: Integrating a Social Robot into the Actor’s Rehearsal Process
papers.authors: Lior Weiner, Sharon Aronson-Lehavi, Goren Gordon
papers.abstract: Effective theatrical rehearsal is essential for actors’ character development, involving intricate cognitive, emotional, and physical processes. Despite well-established traditional techniques that combine individual practice and partner interactions, rehearsal often requires significant time and resources. Emerging digital and robotic technologies present novel opportunities to enhance rehearsal methods; however, their potential as interactive rehearsal aids remains largely unexplored. This research examines the role of a social robot in supporting actors during pre-rehearsal or solo preparation of two scenes from Tennessee Williams’ The Glass Menagerie (1944). Thirty actors with different levels of experience participated in three rehearsal settings: solo practice, rehearsal with a robot playing one character, and rehearsal with the robot alternating between two roles. We evaluated the robot's impact via qualitative responses and self-reports. Thematic analysis indicated that robot-assisted rehearsal improved participants’ experience compared to solo rehearsal, especially among less experienced actors. The robot's role-switching capability offered additional depth appreciated mainly by seasoned performers. These outcomes highlight the promise of social robots as rehearsal tools adapted to the experience of actors.
